hypotheses.statement: Heater has positive steady-state gain: higher constant u yields higher equilibrium y.
Step response has appreciable lag/delay: y takes tens to hundreds of seconds to approach equilibrium.
No large dead zone: even u=0.3-0.5 produces a clear rise compared to u=0.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0-0.1 due to heat loss.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear in u across 0 to 1.
Constant u near 0.5 holds y near target 0.5 at equilibrium.
Sensor noise and short-term fluctuations are small (<~0.01) compared to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag: a first mid-level hold discriminates heating vs no response and measures rise rate and curvature needed for all later control design.

proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain, lag, decay at u=0, linearity, steady-state input for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved; at least three experiments are required before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: hold mid power 0.5 for 200 s to measure heating direction, rate and lag.

hypotheses.statement: Heater has positive steady-state gain: higher constant u yields higher equilibrium y.

Change is weaker actuator: same u>0 gives smaller rise, but u=0 cooling rate/ambient (~0.12-0.20) and delay (~15-30 s) unchanged.
Change is faster outflow / increased heat loss: fall at u=0 is faster than in E2 and equilibrium for same u and ambient are lower.
Change is slower response: increased deadtime/time constant, delay from command change to first response >50-60 s vs ~20 s in E1/E2.
Change is sensor offset/noise: true thermal dynamics unchanged but readings show persistent ~-0.07 to -0.10 bias and/or larger negative dips.
